newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-KOMEN CAPS REMARKABLE YEAR WITH GOLD MEDAL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KOMEN CAPS REMARKABLE YEAR WITH GOLD MEDAL.

text.p: Kenyan Daniel Komen capped a memorable season on Sunday when he destroyed the field in the men's 5,000 metres final after an electrifying change of speed five laps from the finish.

Komen, 21, who missed last year's Atlanta Olympics after failing to make the Kenyan team but produced some brilliant form afterwards, raced away from the rest of the field with two sub-60 second laps,

The Kenyan, who started running at the age of seven when he loped 20 kms to and from school, never looked in danger afterwards, winning in 13 minutes 07.38 seconds ahead of Morocco's Khalid Boulami and Kenya's Tom Nyariki who took silver and bronze respectively.
Despite his absence from the Olympics, Komen won the Grand Prix overall title and took more than four seconds off Algerian Noureddine Morceli's 3,000 metres world record in Rieti, Italy.
Although Athens was his first major championships, Komen ran like a seasoned campaigner, staying out of trouble in the early laps before timing his kick to perfection.
"After seven laps I planned to get away," he said. "It was not easy and I was under a lot of pressure. I stayed behind at first but I was not surprised to win.
"Now I will rest for a day and decide whether I should go for the world record in Zurich."
Former Olympic champion Dieter Baumann of Germany and Nyariki set the pace early on but Komen then ran two laps of 59.38 and 58.38 seconds which split the field apart.

He quickly gained a 30-metre lead over Nyariki and Boulami who were left to battle it out for second and third. The Moroccan made a late burst in the final 100 metres to seal the silver in 13:09.34 with Nyariki third in 13:11.09.
"I expected Komen to go away like this in the last 1,000. He surprised me by doing it so early," Boulami said.
